parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  What is a Ratio?
content: A RATIO compares two or more quantities.
In a class, there are 12 boys and 8 girls.
The ratio of boys to girls is 12 to 8, or 12:8.
A recipe needs 2 cups of flour and 1 cup of sugar.
The ratio of flour to sugar is 2:1.
"For every 2 cups of flour, use 1 cup of sugar."
On a map, 1 cm represents 10 km.
"1 centimeter on the map equals 10 kilometers in real life."
Ratios help us compare and understand relationships!

listening_script.speed_note: Read aloud at a normal, clear pace (85 wpm). Pause 2–3 seconds between sentences. Read the full text twice before students answer questions.
listening_script.text:
A RATIO compares two or more quantities.
Example 1:
In a class, there are 12 boys and 8 girls.
The ratio of boys to girls is 12 to 8, or 12:8.
We can simplify this: 12:8 = 3:2
"For every 3 boys, there are 2 girls."
WAYS TO WRITE A RATIO:
- 3 to 2
- 3:2
- 3/2 (as a fraction)
Example 2:
A recipe needs 2 cups of flour and 1 cup of sugar.
The ratio of flour to sugar is 2:1.
"For every 2 cups of flour, use 1 cup of sugar."
Example 3:
On a map, 1 cm represents 10 km.
The ratio is 1:10.
"1 centimeter on the map equals 10 kilometers in real life."
Ratios help us compare and understand relationships!
dictation: A RATIO compares two or more quantities.

Example 1:
In a class, there are 12 boys and 8 girls.
The ratio of boys to girls is 12 to 8, or 12:8.
